programme.title: Atomic People
programme.desc: The decision by the United States to drop atomic bombs on two Japanese cities, Hiroshima on 6 August 1945 and Nagasaki three days later, was one of the most momentous and destructive in world history. Now, nearly 80 years later, testimony of some of the last 'Hibakusha' survivors of the two atomic bombs is gathered before their voices are lost forever. With an average age of 85, most Hibakusha were children when the bombs were dropped. Archive footage is combined with the personal accounts of this shrinking group, the only people left on Earth to have survived a nuclear bomb and whose experiences continue to affect them to this day.

programme.desc: Actor and comedian John Thomson looks back at the life and work of his friend and comedy colleague, the late and greatly missed Caroline Aherne. programme.title: Caroline Aherne: Queen of Comedy
programme.desc: A celebration of the unique life and talent of Caroline Aherne, featuring unseen photographs and contributions from a cast of her lifelong friends, including Steve Coogan, John Thompson, Craig Cash and producer Andy Harries.

programme.title: Storyville
programme.sub-title: The Hijacker Who Vanished: The Mystery of DB Cooper
programme.desc: A mysterious fugitive, a hijacked airplane and a daring mid-air escape. This is the extraordinary, real-life tale of one of the greatest unsolved heists in American history and a case that has taunted the FBI for decades.

programme.title: Timothy Spall: Back at Sea
programme.desc: Timothy and Shane take their barge to three different countries and the Isle of Man. From Whitehaven, where Timothy learns about the pirate John Paul Jones, they steam over to Douglas to visit his son, actor Rafe Spall, who is there to work on BBC2's `The Shadow Line'. Next, they visit a city Tim loves dearly, Belfast, and a special pub he says is the finest drinking establishment in the English-speaking world.

programme.title: The Lakes with Paul Rose
programme.desc: Explorer Paul Rose digs out his rucksack and heads for Windermere. The National Park attracts 18 million visitors each year, and is now a World Heritage Site. Paul joins the crowds and finds out why the early tourists thought the Lakes was one of the most dangerous spots in the country. He also plunges into the world of long-distance swimming and helps the staff who run the boats on the lake.

programme.title: James May at the Edge of Space
programme.desc: James May always wanted to be an astronaut. Now, 40 years after the first Apollo landings, he gets a chance to fly to the edge of space in a U2 spy plane, but first he will have to undergo three gruelling days of training with the US Air Force and learn to use a space suit to stay alive in air so thin it can kill in an instant.

programme.title: Days That Shook the World
programme.desc: Sailors, naval officers, nurses and pilots recall the 1941 attack on Hawaii, bringing to life the extraordinary 24 hours that would change the course of world history.

programme.title: Timothy Spall: Back at Sea
programme.desc: As summer comes to a close, Timothy Spall's trip around the coast of his beloved Britain reaches the halfway mark. He encounters several Scottish ports and islands, but mostly in the famous Scottish misty drizzle. Before the weather worsens he winds his way through the Scottish western islands and takes his barge Princess Matilda back to her roots by venturing up the Caledonian Canal.

programme.title: The Lakes with Paul Rose
programme.desc: Explorer Paul Rose packs his waterproofs and heads for Derwentwater and Borrowdale. Borrowdale is officially the wettest place in England, and he meets those who have battled against flooding and have learned to live with extreme weather events. Along the way, he tells the story of Millican Dalton, the Professor of Adventure, who ran his own expeditions in the Lake District more than 70 years ago. Paul also heads for the summit of Great Gable, one of the Lake's best known peaks.

programme.title: Japan's Master of Restoration
programme.desc: The father and son undertake the restoration of a ceramic horse from the Edo period. A previous restoration is now showing signs of age, and a new approach is needed to give the horse back its stallion stance.

programme.title: Around the World in 80 Treasures
programme.desc: Dan Cruickshank visits the Dogon people and sees some masks and wall paintings.

programme.title: Tribe
programme.desc: Bruce Parry spends six weeks with the Adi people of Arunachal Pradesh in the Himalayas, learns how to hunt, and takes part in sacrificial ceremonies with the tribe of former warriors, who were cut off from civilisation for centuries.

programme.title: Sherlock
programme.desc: Contemporary crime drama, based on the novels by Arthur Conan Doyle. A war hero, invalided home from Afghanistan, meets a strange but charismatic genius who is looking for a flatmate. It is London, 2010, and Dr Watson and Sherlock Holmes are meeting for the first time. A string of impossible suicides has Scotland Yard baffled - and only one man can help.

programme.title: Mark Lawson Talks to...
programme.desc: Mark Lawson talks to writer, actor and comedian Mark Gatiss about his life, career and fulfilling childhood dreams. Gatiss explores formative memories of growing up opposite a psychiatric hospital in County Durham, admits the difficulty of coming out as a gay man and reveals why his role in the British film flop `Sex Lives of the Potato Men' was the biggest mistake of his career.

programme.desc: Winnipeg and Dallas meet in Game 1 of a West semifinal. Mikko Rantanen scored a third-period hat trick in Game 7 as the Stars ousted his old club in the Avalanche, while the Jets dispatched the Blues in double overtime after a last-second tying goal.

programme.title: NHL Hockey
programme.desc: The Jets try to bounce back against the Stars, down 1-0 entering Game 2 of their West semifinal. Mikko Rantanen continued his scorching-hot playoffs, scoring a natural hat trick for Dallas in a 3-2 Game 1 win over Winnipeg. Rantanen has eight goals.

programme.title: NHL Hockey
programme.desc: Dallas hosts Winnipeg for Game 3 of their Western Conference semifinal. Connor Hellebuyck recorded his fourth career postseason shutout to help the Jets take Game 2 and even the series 1-1. Nikolaj Ehlers (WPG) had three points in the 4-0 victory.

programme.title: NHL Hockey
programme.desc: The Jets try to even their Western Conference semifinal with the Stars in Game 4 from Texas. Mikko Rantanen continued his spectacular postseason with a goal and two assists as Dallas took a 5-2 victory and a 2-1 series advantage in Game 3.

programme.title: NHL Hockey
programme.desc: The Jets and Stars play Game 5 of this Western Conference semifinal. Winnipeg has lost nine straight playoff games on the road after Dallas won back-to-back at home to take a 3-1 series lead. The Stars seek a third straight trip to the West finals.

programme.title: NHL Hockey
programme.desc: The Stars try a second time to ground the Jets in Game 6 of their Western Conference semifinal. Connor Hellebuyck turned away all 22 Dallas shots in Game 5 and Nikolaj Ehlers scored twice to power Winnipeg to a 4-0 victory to stave off elimination.
